# With Giving Day we broke records in philanthropy

**With nearly 60 million pesos raised, this year's Giving Day was the most successful in terms of funds raised. The resources will go to** [**Vamos Pa'lante**](https://www.eafit.edu.co/becas-y-financiacion/vamos-pa-lante) **, a program that provides scholarships to talented students.**

**Thanks to the 500 people and 18 partner organizations that participated in this event. Thanks also to the members of the Partner Campus student group, the University Symphony Orchestra, and everyone who will continue to join us in strengthening our talent community.**

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias)
- With Giving Day we broke records in philanthropy

![Image: With Giving Day we broke records in philanthropy](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/f2e23580-2a23-4b6d-99f5-adcfcdb3a9e1/web/record-filantropia.jpg?crop=yes&k=c&w=823&h=450&itok=qyBTL8F-)

Giving Day took place on October 17th throughout the day at EAFIT's main campus. On November 2nd, Partner Campus held Hono, an activity as part of Giving Day.

So significant was his support for the arts, the protection of talented young people, and culture in general, that his name became synonymous with those who selflessly contribute to the development of society in various fields: Gaius Maecenas. This confidant and advisor to Augustus, the first Roman emperor, is the earliest example of a practice that continues to this day: patronage.

If it weren't for figures like Gaius Maecenas, monarchs, bourgeois, or religious leaders, many of the representative works of the arts, including musical ones, might not exist, as Susana Palacio David, manager of the EAFIT Symphony Orchestra, points out.

This group is a powerful testament to the importance of patronage in education. Susana explains that nearly 80 percent of the members of this EAFIT-based group have studied with the support of scholarships. These are the same musicians who, on November 2nd, gave the closing concert for [Giving Day](https://www.eafit.edu.co/filantropia/iniciativas/giving-day) , one of EAFIT's flagship philanthropic activities .

For the past five years, the University has held this event to promote a culture of philanthropy within the EAFIT community. This goal has been achieved thanks to the involvement of partners such as Partner Campus, a student group at the University that, for the first time this year, joined the event with various fundraising activities. The closing event, titled "Hono," featured a performance by the Symphony Orchestra. While the orchestra played, a QR code for donations appeared on the screen in the Founders Auditorium.

These contributions helped the fundraising effort reach nearly 60 million pesos collected during this Giving Day. “We want to extend our special thanks to the entire community for their enthusiastic participation in transforming education this year. Together, we have achieved the highest amount raised in the history of our event, and this would not have been possible without the invaluable support of each and every one of you,” says Amalia Londoño Duque, Head of Philanthropy at EAFIT.

This was also the Giving Day with the highest number of participants: 500 people and 18 partners. Hence the words of gratitude from Isabel Gómez Yepes, Director of Institutional Development and Partnerships: “We are very grateful. Together, we are maximizing this community of talent. This is proof that when we unite, we achieve wonderful things. We are all convinced that we must join this cause so that more people can have access to the University and be part of a community of talent that we know transforms everything it touches.” The partners she refers to are restaurants and brands such as Aldea Nikei, Coffee House, Fire House, Pmiento'z, 123 Wok, Clap Burgers, El Correo / Amada, Ganso & Castor, Juniper, La Hora del Venado, Malicia, Monterojo, Olivia, Parmessano, Newo, Tahiti, Tau House, and Uau.

Nearly 20 percent of EAFIT students study on some type of scholarship, and the goal is to expand those opportunities. The funds raised during Giving Day will be used for this purpose. They will be added to [Vamos Pa'lante](https://www.eafit.edu.co/becas-y-financiacion/vamos-pa-lante) , a program created by W Radio and the University of the Andes, in which EAFIT and three other universities participate. This campaign focuses on undergraduate students from their third semester onward who are at risk of dropping out due to financial difficulties.

The University joined [Vamos Pa'lante](https://www.eafit.edu.co/becas-y-financiacion/vamos-pa-lante) in 2021. During 2023, in both semesters, the beneficiaries are 96, who were given tuition assistance, support for living expenses and in some cases for both needs.

The option to donate to this initiative is active. Therefore, Amalia's invitation, especially to EAFIT graduates, is to remember that we are all part of this EAFIT talent community and can help strengthen it. "All your contributions are invaluable and allow us to continue promoting a culture of philanthropy and the importance of access for social mobility," she concludes.

metadata.og:description: Fue tan importante el impulso que le dio a las artes, a la protección de los jóvenes talentosos y a la cultura en general, que su nombre se convirtió en sinónimo de quienes aportan de manera desinteresada al desarrollo de la sociedad desde diferentes ámbitos: Cayo Mecenas. Este confidente y asesor de Augusto, el primer emperador romano, es el referente más antiguo de una práctica que siga viva, el mecenazgo.
